brief: I read 52 books in 12 months as a founder. These 6 changed how I operate.

slots.eyebrow: ONE YEAR FIFTY-TWO BOOKS SIX LESSONS
slots.subtitle: I read fifty-two books in one year. These six changed how I build and decide daily.
slots.preview1: The systems book that replaced my to-do list
slots.preview2: The psychology read that fixed my pricing
slots.preview3: The memoir that reframed failure entirely

slots.title: Small habits
slots.subtitle: Clear’s framework turned my daily routines into compounding founder leverage.
slots.insight1Body: Attach reading to morning coffee before checking any metrics dashboard.
slots.insight2Body: Label yourself reader first; the pages follow the self-image shift.
slots.insight3Body: Fall in love with the process so output becomes inevitable and steady.
slots.pullQuote: You do not rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems.

slots.title: Wealth is
slots.subtitle: Housel taught me that financial success is more psychology than IQ.
slots.insight1Body: Keep cash reserves high enough to sleep through any market downturn.
slots.insight2Body: Control the gap between ego and income to outlast competitors always.
slots.insight3Body: A few bets in a lifetime generate most returns; stay patient.
slots.pullQuote: Spending money to show people how much money you have is the fastest way to have less money.

slots.title: Monopoly beats
slots.subtitle: Thiel’s contrarian question forced me to build where others saw saturation.
slots.insight1Body: Look for truths most people believe are false but you know otherwise.
slots.insight2Body: It is better to be the final entity that captures the market.
slots.insight3Body: Superior product without distribution dies quietly in the digital wilderness.
slots.pullQuote: Competition is for losers. If you are not monopoly, you are competing.

slots.title: Embrace the
slots.subtitle: Horowitz showed me that founder strength is forged in impossible moments.
slots.insight1Body: Focus anxiety only on things you can actually control and change.
slots.insight2Body: Layoffs are management failures; carry the burden without crushing your team.
slots.insight3Body: The only way out is through; endure longer than the market expects.
slots.pullQuote: By far the most difficult skill I learned as CEO was the ability to manage my own psychology.

slots.title: Decisions are
slots.subtitle: Duke taught me to separate decision quality from outcome luck in real time.
slots.insight1Body: A good process can yield bad outcomes; judge the method, not luck.
slots.insight2Body: Invite dissenting voices to tear apart your strongest strategic assumptions early.
slots.insight3Body: Replace certainty language with confidence percentages to expose real risk levels.
slots.pullQuote: What makes a decision great is not that it has a great outcome.

slots.title: Focus is
slots.subtitle: Newport proved that undistracted blocks are the only real competitive advantage left.
slots.insight1Body: Protect four-hour morning windows for hard creative work above all else.
slots.insight2Body: Remove attention auctions from your phone to reclaim three hours daily.
slots.insight3Body: Track real output per session instead of vanity tasks completed by noon.
slots.pullQuote: Clarity about what matters provides clarity about what does not.

slots.ctaBody: These six books rebuilt my founder operating system. Which one will you read first?
